chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his wife at the time of sacrifice, before he visited the House (Kaaba). He said, 'He sheds blood.'

key_terms.زُورَ الْبَيْتَ: Visited the House (referring to Tawaf al-Ziyarah, the essential pillar of Hajj)
key_terms.ضَحَى: Sacrifice (referring to the time of the Hajj sacrifice or the state of being muhrim)
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُ دَمًا: Sheds blood (idiomatic legal term for the obligation of slaughtering a sacrificial animal as expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (kaffarah) for a pilgrim who has sexual intercourse with his wife before completing Tawaf al-Ziyarah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that sexual intercourse during Hajj before Tawaf al-Ziyarah incurs the penalty of 'shedding blood' (yuhiriqu daman), which Shia jurists interpret as the obligatory slaughter of a camel, cow, or sheep. This ruling highlights the severity of breaking the sanctity of the Ihram state through major acts, distinguishing it from minor infractions, and underscores the principle that the expiation is tied to the specific stage of the pilgrimage rites.
